convertibility_reason: Uses divergence detection which is custom logic (not a built-in indicator), combined with EMA and RSI filters. Divergence requires multi-bar pattern recognition (swing high/low detection and comparison across price and indicator) that cannot be mapped to a single built-in indicator call. Multiple companion EAs and alerts suggest complex signal coordination.

derived_values.name: Bearish divergence: price makes higher high while RSI makes lower high
Bullish divergence: price makes lower low while RSI makes higher low

other_exits: RSI close condition: close sell when RSI exits overbought zone or close buy when RSI exits oversold zone; divergence signal on opposite side closes existing position

custom_logic_notes: Divergence detection scans for swing highs/lows over a lookback window and compares price swing direction against RSI swing direction. A bearish divergence (price higher high, RSI lower high) triggers sell-only logic in the sell EA. A bullish divergence (price lower low, RSI higher low) triggers buy-only logic in the buy EA. The strategy is split into separate buy-only and sell-only EAs, likely for independent optimization or to run on separate charts. The 'close sell only' and 'close buy only' variants use RSI levels to close positions rather than fixed SL/TP. The Alert variant emits notifications instead of placing trades.
python_conversion_notes: Divergence detection is the hardest part to convert - requires swing point identification (zigzag-like logic) across price and RSI series, comparing direction of successive swing highs/lows. No single indicator call reproduces this. Must implement: 1) Swing high/low finder using lookback windows, 2) Divergence validator checking if price and RSI swings diverge in direction, 3) RSI overbought/oversold close logic for the 'close' variants. The split into buy-only/sell-only EAs suggests each direction should be a separate signal class in Python. EMA crossover is a secondary filter/confirmation, not the primary trigger. Pay attention to the 'close' variants which use RSI level exits instead of or in addition to fixed SL/TP.
